findings.expected: The declared Firefox minimum versions support every manifest key and permission API used by v0.5
findings.actual: The source declared Firefox 109.0 while data_collection_permissions starts at Firefox desktop 140 and Android 142; web-ext also flagged permissions.request as unsupported on Firefox Android 109
findings.resolution: Raised the generated desktop minimum to 140.0 and Android minimum to 142.0, then added a manifest regression test and rebuilt both Firefox ZIPs
evidence: Before fix: web-ext 10.3.0 reported 20 warnings including KEY_FIREFOX_UNSUPPORTED_BY_MIN_VERSION, KEY_FIREFOX_ANDROID_UNSUPPORTED_BY_MIN_VERSION, and ANDROID_INCOMPATIBLE_API
After fix: web-ext 10.3.0 reported 0 errors and 0 Firefox/minimum-version/API compatibility warnings
Mozilla Firefox built-in consent documentation identifies desktop 140 and Android 142 as the supported baselines

findings.expected: AMO lint findings are recorded and reviewed rather than silently treated as a clean report
findings.actual: web-ext reports 15 UNSAFE_VAR_ASSIGNMENT warnings in bundled UI/React code and no errors
findings.resolution: No runtime behavior was changed in this artifact task; source review confirmed untrusted display names, handles, snippets, reasons, notes, IDs, and avatar URLs are escaped or allowlisted before template insertion. Retain the warnings for final adversarial review.

findings.expected: A fresh Firefox profile can warm an empty local index without emitting an unhandled runtime error
findings.actual: requestBackgroundSync discarded the Promise returned by chrome.runtime.sendMessage. When warmLocalIndex ran inside the Firefox background itself, Firefox rejected it with 'Could not establish connection. Receiving end does not exist.'
findings.resolution: requestBackgroundSync now awaits and consumes both synchronous and asynchronous unavailable-receiver failures; a targeted regression covers Firefox's rejected Promise
evidence: Before fix: the real Firefox browser console recorded two background.js missing-receiver errors during popup/health startup
After fix: the same isolated Firefox flow reports zero extension-origin errors
Complete extension suite passed 27/27, including background sync request consumes Firefox's missing-receiver rejection

findings.expected: A forced options-page reload tears down extension API listeners without browser-internal noise
findings.actual: Firefox 152.0.6 logged one sendRemoveListener on closed conduit message from resource://gre/modules/ConduitsChild.sys.mjs while destroying the old extension page context
findings.resolution: Recorded separately from extension-origin errors; storage persistence, the reloaded page, and the restored setting all completed successfully
